title: Reflection from a 3 eV potential step
caption: Above the step (E > V₀ = 3 eV) the wave still reflects partially: R = ((k₁ − k₂)/(k₁ + k₂))² with k ∝ √E and k₂ ∝ √(E − V₀). At E = 5 eV, k₁/k₂ = √(5/2) = 1.58 and R = 0.05, so 5% of the electrons bounce back; T = 1 − R = 0.95. R falls as E rises but never reaches zero, and at E = V₀ all are reflected.
alt: Graph of reflection and transmission probabilities against electron energy from 3 to 12 electronvolts for a 3 electronvolt step: reflection falls from 1 to 0.05 at 5 electronvolts and keeps falling; transmission rises correspondingly.
description: The horizontal axis is the electron energy E in eV, above the 3 eV step; the vertical axis is the probability.
R = ((√E − √(E − 3))/(√E + √(E − 3)))² (the ratio k₂/k₁ = √(1 − V₀/E)). At E = 3 eV, R = 1.
At E = 5 eV, R = 0.05: about 5% reflected, 95% transmitted.
As E grows, R decreases towards zero but a classical particle would never be reflected: this is a wave effect.
